sanskrit: samīkṣya vimalaṃ vyoma gatavidyudbalāhakam sārasāravasaṃghuṣṭaṃ ramyajyotsnānulepanam
english: Having observed the clear sky, emptied of lightning and clouds, resounding with the calls of sārasas and āravas, smeared as it were with lovely moonlight,

sanskrit: samṛddhārthaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ mandadharmārthasaṃgraham atyartham asatāṃ mārgam ekāntagatamānasaṃ
english: and having observed Sugrīva, his object accomplished, but slack in the pursuit of duty and purpose, exceedingly gone the way of the ignoble, his mind wholly bent on pleasure,

sanskrit: nivṛttakāryaṃ siddhārthaṃ pramadābhirataṃ sadā prāptavantam abhipretān sarvān eva manorathān
english: his tasks discharged, his aims fulfilled, always delighting in women, having obtained all the desires of his heart,

sanskrit: svāṃ ca pātnīm abhipretāṃ tārāṃ cāpi samīpsitām viharantam ahorātraṃ kṛtārthaṃ vigatajvalam
english: sporting day and night with his own beloved wife and with Tārā whom he desired, having achieved his end, free from fever,

sanskrit: krīḍantam iva deveśaṃ nandane 'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ mantriṣu nyastakāryaṃ ca mantriṇām anavekṣakam
english: sporting like the lord of gods in Nandana with hosts of Apsarases, having delegated his affairs to his ministers, and not supervising those ministers—

sanskrit: utsannarājyasaṃdeśaṃ kāmavṛttam avasthitam niścitārtho 'rthatattvajñaḥ kāladharmaviśeṣavit
english: having abandoned his royal commands, remaining under the sway of desire — Hanumān, who had resolved on his purpose, who knew the true nature of things and the special significance of time and duty,

sanskrit: prasādya vākyair madhurair hetumadbhir manoramaiḥ vākyavid vākyatattvajñaṃ harīśaṃ mārutātmajaḥ
english: having propitiated with sweet, reasoned, and pleasing words the lord of the monkeys who was skilled in speech and knew the truth of language — the son of Māruta,

sanskrit: hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca sāmadharmārthanītimat praṇayaprītisaṃyuktaṃ viśvāsakṛtaniścayam harīśvaram upāgamya hanumān vākyam abravīt
english: approaching the lord of the monkeys, spoke words that were beneficial, truthful, and wholesome, in accord with the polity of conciliation, duty and purpose, joined with affection and love, and designed to inspire confidence.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ prāptaṃ yaśaś caiva kaulī śrīr abhivarthitā mitrāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ śeṣas tad bhavān kartum arhati
english: "Kingdom has been gained, glory as well, the ancestral prosperity has increased; what remains is the gathering in of friends — that, Your Lordship, it is right for you to do."

sanskrit: yo hi mitreṣu kālajñaḥ satataṃ sādhu vartate tasya rājyaṃ ca kīrtiś ca pratāpaś cābhivardhate
english: "For the one who is wise regarding timing and always behaves rightly toward friends — his kingdom, his fame, and his majesty continually increase."

sanskrit: yasya kośaś ca daṇḍaś ca mitrāṇy ātmā ca bhūmipa samavetāni sarvāṇi sa rājyaṃ mahad aśnute
english: "O lord of the earth, he whose treasury, power of punishment, allies, and self are all united — he enjoys great kingship."

sanskrit: tad bhavān vṛttasaṃpannaḥ sthitaḥ pathi niratyaye mitrārtham abhinītārthaṃ yathāvat kartum arhati
english: "Therefore you, endowed with virtue, standing on the blameless path, ought properly to fulfill what is well-ordered and meant for the sake of your friend."

sanskrit: yas tu kālavyatīteṣu mitrakāryeṣu vartate sa kṛtvā mahato 'py arthān na mitrārthena yujyate
english: "But he who attends to a friend's affairs when the time has passed — even if he achieves great things, he will not be joined to the fruit of friendship."

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ rāghavasyaitad vaidehyāḥ parimārgaṇam tad idaṃ vīra kāryaṃ te kālātītam ariṃdama
english: "Let the search for Rāghava's Vaidehī be carried out. O hero, O subduer of foes, this task of yours has passed its proper time."

sanskrit: na ca kālam atītaṃ te nivedayati kālavit tvaramāṇo 'pi san prājñas tava rājan vaśānugaḥ
english: "A wise man who knows the right moment, though eager himself, does not report to you that the time has passed, O king — he who follows your command."

sanskrit: kulasya ketuḥ sphītasya dīrghabandhuś ca rāghavaḥ aprameyaprabhāvaś ca svayaṃ cāpratimo guṇaiḥ
english: "Rāghava is the banner of his prosperous lineage, a friend for long ages, of immeasurable power, and himself without equal in virtues."

sanskrit: tasya tvaṃ kuru vai kāryaṃ pūrvaṃ tena kṛtaṃ tava harīśvara hariśreṣṭhān ājñāpayitum arhati
english: "Do his task — what was done for you first by him. O lord of monkeys, you should command the foremost of monkeys."

sanskrit: na hi tāvad bhavet kālo vyatītaś codanād ṛte coditasya hi kāryasya bhavet kālavyatikramaḥ
english: "For the time would not have passed without a prompting; but for a task already prompted, there could indeed be a transgression of time."

sanskrit: akartur api kāryasya bhavān kartā harīśvara kiṃ punaḥ pratikartus te rājyena ca dhanena ca
english: "You, O lord of monkeys, are the doer even for one who has done nothing; how much more so for him who has repaid you with kingdom and wealth."

sanskrit: śaktimān asi vikrānto vānararṣka gaṇeśvara kartuṃ dāśaratheḥ prītim ājñāyāṃ kiṃ nu sajjase
english: "You are capable and valiant, O lord of troops of monkeys and bears; why then do you hesitate at the command to bring joy to the son of Daśaratha?"

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalu śarair śaktaḥ surāsuramahoragān vaśe dāśarathiḥ kartuṃ tvatpratijñāṃ tu kāṅkṣate
english: "Indeed, the son of Daśaratha is certainly capable with his arrows of bringing gods, demons, and great serpents under his sway; yet he waits upon your promise."

sanskrit: prāṇatyāgāviśaṅkena kṛtaṃ tena tava priyam tasya mārgāma vaidehīṃ pṛthivyām api cāmbare
english: "Without hesitation in abandoning even life, he did what was dear to you; let us search for his Vaidehī — on earth or in the sky."

sanskrit: na devā na ca gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ na ca yakṣā bhayaṃ tasya kuryuḥ kim uta rākṣasāḥ
english: "Neither gods nor Gandharvas, neither Asuras nor hosts of Maruts, nor Yakṣas could cause him fear — let alone Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tad evaṃ śaktiyuktasya pūrvaṃ priyakṛtas tathā rāmasyārhasi piṅgeśa kartuṃ sarvātmanā priyam
english: "Since he is thus endowed with power, and since he had previously done what was dear to you, O lord of tawny monkeys, you ought with your whole soul to do what is dear to Rāma."

sanskrit: nādhastād avanau nāpsu gatir nopari cāmbare kasya cit sajjate 'smākaṃ kapīśvara tavājñayā
english: "By your command, O lord of monkeys, none of our movements is impeded — not below on the earth, not in the waters, not above in the sky."

sanskrit: tad ājñāpaya kaḥ kiṃ te kṛte vasatu kutra cit harayo hy apradhṛṣyās te santi koṭyagrato 'nagha
english: "Therefore give the command — who shall dwell where and for what purpose; your monkeys, invincible, number crores upon crores, O sinless one."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kāle sādhuniveditam sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṃpannaś cakāra matim uttamām
english: Having heard his words, well-spoken at the right moment, Sugrīva, endowed with good judgment, formed a most excellent resolve.

sanskrit: sa saṃdideśābhimataṃ nīlaṃ nityakṛtodyamam dikṣu sarvāsu sarveṣāṃ sainyānām upasaṃgrahe
english: He commanded the trusted Nīla, ever diligent, to gather together the armies from all directions.

sanskrit: yathā senā samagrā me yūthapālāś ca sarvaśaḥ samāgacchanty asaṃgena senāgrāṇi tathā kuru
english: "Arrange things so that my entire army and all the troop-leaders assemble without delay, together with their vanguards."

sanskrit: ye tv antapālāḥ plavagāḥ śīghragā vyavasāyinaḥ samānayantu te sainyaṃ tvaritāḥ śāsanān mama svayaṃ cānantaraṃ sainyaṃ bhavān evānupaśyatu
english: "And let those monkey border-guards who are swift and resolute quickly summon the troops by my command; and you yourself thereafter shall personally review the army."

sanskrit: tripañcarātrād ūrdhvaṃ yaḥ prāpnuyān neha vānaraḥ tasya prāṇāntiko daṇḍo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: "Whatever monkey fails to arrive here within fifteen days shall suffer the penalty of death — in this matter no deliberation need be made."

sanskrit: harīṃś ca vṛddhān upayātu sāṅgado bhavān mamājñām adhikṛtya niścitām iti vyavasthāṃ haripuṃgaveśvaro vidhāya veśma praviveśa vīryavān
english: "And together with Aṅgada, let the elder monkeys approach with my command firmly established in view." Having thus arranged affairs, the mighty lord, chief among the foremost of monkeys, entered his palace.

sanskrit: guhāṃ praviṣṭe sugrīve vimukte gagane ghanaiḥ varṣarātroṣito rāmaḥ kāmaśokābhipīḍitaḥ
english: When Sugrīva had entered his cave-palace and the sky was emptied of clouds, Rāma, who had spent the rainy nights waiting, tormented by desire and grief,

sanskrit: pāṇḍuraṃ gaganaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimalaṃ candramaṇḍalam śāradīṃ rajanīṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā jyotsnānulepanām
english: seeing the pale sky, the clear orb of the moon, and the autumnal night smeared as it were with moonlight,

sanskrit: kāmavṛttaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ naṣṭāṃ ca janakātmajām buddhvā kālam atītaṃ ca mumoha paramāturaḥ
english: and reflecting that Sugrīva was absorbed in pleasure, that the daughter of Janaka was lost, and that the time had passed — fell into a swoon, exceedingly afflicted.

sanskrit: sa tu saṃjñām upāgamya muhūrtān matimān punaḥ manaḥsthām api vaidehīṃ cintayām āsa rāghavaḥ
english: But after a moment, regaining consciousness, the wise Rāghava began to think of Vaidehī who dwelt only in his mind.

sanskrit: āsīnaḥ parvatasyāgre hemadhātuvibhūṣite śāradaṃ gaganaṃ dṛṣṭva jagāma manasā priyām
english: Seated on the summit of the mountain adorned with golden minerals, gazing at the autumnal sky, he went in his mind to his beloved.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca vimalaṃ vyoma gatavidyudbalāhakam sārasāravasaṃghuṣṭaṃ vilalāpārtayā girā
english: And seeing the clear sky, emptied of lightning and clouds, resounding with the cries of sārasas and āravas, he lamented with a voice full of pain.

sanskrit: sārasāravasaṃnādaiḥ sārasāravanādinī yāśrame ramate bālā sādya me ramate katham
english: "The young woman who used to delight in the hermitage, herself calling out like the sārasas and āravas — how does she delight today without me?"

sanskrit: puṣpitāṃś cāsanān dṛṣṭvā kāñcanān iva nirmalān kathaṃ sa ramate bālā paśyantī mām apaśyatī
english: "Seeing the flowering aśana trees, pure as gold — how does that young woman delight, beholding them yet not seeing me?"

sanskrit: yā purā kalahaṃsānāṃ svareṇa kalabhāṣiṇī budhyate cārusarvāṅgī sādya me budhyate katham
english: "She who once awakened at the sweet speech of the kalahaṃsas, herself sweet-voiced, beautiful in every limb — how does she awaken today without me?"

sanskrit: niḥsvanaṃ cakravākānāṃ niśamya sahacāriṇām puṇḍarīkaviśālākṣī katham eṣā bhaviṣyati
english: "Having heard the cries of the cakravāka birds with their companions — she whose eyes are wide as a white lotus — how will she fare?"

sanskrit: sarāṃsi sarito vāpīḥ kānanāni vanāni ca tāṃ vinā mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ caran nādya sukhaṃ labhe
english: "Wandering among lakes, rivers, pools, forests, and groves — without her, whose eyes are like a fawn's, I find no happiness today."

sanskrit: api tāṃ madviyogāc ca saukumāryāc ca bhāminīm na dūraṃ pīḍayet kāmaḥ śaradguṇanirantaraḥ
english: "Surely separation from me and her own delicateness must not long torment that passionate woman — love continuously accompanied by autumnal qualities."

sanskrit: evamādi naraśreṣṭho vilalāpa nṛpātmajaḥ vihaṃga iva sāraṅgaḥ salilaṃ tridaśeśvarāt
english: Thus and in like vein the best of men, that prince, lamented — like a sāranga bird seeking water from the lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: tataś cañcūrya ramyeṣu phalārthī girisānuṣu dadarśa paryupāvṛtto lakṣmīvāṃl lakṣmaṇo 'grajam
english: Then, having roamed the lovely mountain slopes in search of fruit and turning back, the glorious Lakṣmaṇa saw his elder brother.

sanskrit: taṃ cintayā duḥsahayā parītaṃ visaṃjñam ekaṃ vijane manasvī bhrātur viṣādāt paritāpadīnaḥ samīkṣya saumitrir uvāca rāmam
english: Seeing him overwhelmed by unbearable grief, barely conscious, alone in a deserted place, the high-souled son of Sumitrā, distressed and pained by his brother's despair, spoke to Rāma:

sanskrit: kim ārya kāmasya vaśaṃgatena kim ātmapauruṣyaparābhavena ayaṃ sadā saṃhṛiyate samādhiḥ kim atra yogena nivartitena
english: "Why, noble one, surrender to the power of desire? Why overpower your own manly strength? This steadiness of mind is always to be gathered in — what is accomplished here by abandoning such discipline?"

sanskrit: kriyābhiyogaṃ manasaḥ prasādaṃ samādhiyogānugataṃ ca kālam sahāyasāmarthyam adīnasattva svakarmahetuṃ ca kuruṣva hetum
english: "Apply yourself to action, to the tranquility of mind, to the time suited to disciplined effort, to the capacity of your allies — O you of undaunted spirit, make the cause of your own deeds your motive."

sanskrit: na jānakī mānavavaṃśanātha tvayā sanāthā sulabhā pareṇa na cāgnicūḍāṃ jvalitām upetya na dahyate vīravarārha kaś cit
english: "O lord of the human lineage, Jānakī is not easily gained by another while she has you as her protector; and approaching a blazing fire crowned with flame, no one, O you worthy of the foremost of heroes, goes unburned."

sanskrit: salakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇam apradhṛṣyaṃ svabhāvajaṃ vākyam uvāca rāmaḥ hitaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca nayaprasaktaṃ sasāmadharmārthasamāhitaṃ ca
english: Then Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, spoke to the indomitable Lakṣmaṇa a natural word, both beneficial and wholesome, attached to prudent policy and composed with conciliation, duty, and purpose:

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayaṃ kāryam avekṣitavyaṃ kriyāviśeṣo hy anuvartitavyaḥ nanu pravṛttasya durāsadasya kumārakāryasya phalaṃ na cintyam
english: "The task must undoubtedly be attended to; indeed the particular undertaking must be pursued; surely for a difficult task once set in motion, the fruit need not be anxiously considered — it follows in course."

sanskrit: atha padmapalāśākṣīṃ maithilīm anucintayan uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Then, brooding upon Maithilī whose eyes are like lotus petals, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa with a face that had grown parched:

sanskrit: tarpayitvā sahasrākṣaḥ salilena vasuṃdharām nirvartayitvā sasyāni kṛtakarmā vyavasthitaḥ
english: "The thousand-eyed Indra, having satisfied the earth with water, having caused the crops to ripen, stands established having done his work.

sanskrit: snigdhagambhīranirghoṣāḥ śailadrumapurogamāḥ visṛjya salilaṃ meghāḥ pariśrāntā nṛpātmaja
english: "The clouds, their sound deep and resonant, with mountains and trees preceding them, having released their waters, are now exhausted, O prince.

sanskrit: nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ śyāmīkṛtvā diśo daśa vimadā iva mātaṅgāḥ śāntavegāḥ payodharāḥ
english: "Dark as petals of the blue lotus, having darkened all ten directions, the rain-clouds, like elephants out of rut, have quieted their rush.

sanskrit: jalagarbhā mahāvegāḥ kuṭajārjunagandhinaḥ caritvā viratāḥ saumya vṛṣṭivātāḥ samudyatāḥ
english: "The rain-winds, laden with water, of great speed, fragrant with kuṭaja and arjuna blossoms, having coursed their way, have ceased, O gentle one, though they were fully roused.

sanskrit: ghanānāṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca mayūrāṇāṃ ca lakṣmaṇa nādaḥ prasravaṇānāṃ ca praśāntaḥ sahasānagha
english: "The sound of the clouds, of elephants, of peacocks, and of mountain torrents, O Lakṣmaṇa — O sinless one — has suddenly grown still.

sanskrit: abhivṛṣṭā mahāmeghair nirmalāś citrasānavaḥ anuliptā ivābhānti girayaś candraraśmibhiḥ
english: "Drenched by the great clouds, the mountains with their varied slopes shine clear, gleaming as if anointed with the rays of the moon.

sanskrit: darśayanti śarannadyaḥ pulināni śanaiḥ śanaiḥ navasaṃgamasavrīḍā jaghanānīva yoṣitaḥ
english: "The autumnal rivers slowly, slowly reveal their sandbanks — like women bashful at a new union revealing their hips.

sanskrit: prasannasalilāḥ saumya kurarībhir vināditāḥ cakravākagaṇākīrṇā vibhānti salilāśayāḥ
english: "The bodies of water, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa, their waters clear, resounding with the cries of kurara birds, and filled with flocks of cakravākas, shine beautifully.

sanskrit: anyonyabaddhavairāṇāṃ jigīṣūṇāṃ nṛpātmaja udyogasamayaḥ saumya pārthivānām upasthitaḥ
english: "For those kings who are bound together in mutual enmity and eager for victory, O prince, O gentle one, the season of enterprise has arrived.

sanskrit: iyaṃ sā prathamā yātrā pārthivānāṃ nṛpātmaja na ca paśyāmi sugrīvam udyogaṃ vā tathāvidham
english: "This is the foremost season of campaign for kings, O prince — yet I do not see Sugrīva, nor any such effort on his part.

sanskrit: catvāro vārṣikā māsā gatā varṣaśatopamāḥ mama śokābhitaptasya saumya sītām apaśyataḥ
english: "The four months of the rains have passed, each seeming like a hundred years to me, scorched by grief as I am, not seeing Sītā, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: priyāvihīne duḥkhārte hṛtarājye vivāsite kṛpāṃ na kurute rājā sugrīvo mayi lakṣmaṇa
english: "Bereft of my beloved, afflicted by sorrow, my kingdom taken, banished from home — yet king Sugrīva shows no compassion toward me, O Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: anātho hṛtarājyo 'yaṃ rāvaṇena ca dharṣitaḥ dīno dūragṛhaḥ kāmī māṃ caiva śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "Without a protector, his kingdom stolen, humiliated by Rāvaṇa, wretched, far from home, maddened with desire — he came to me as his refuge.

sanskrit: ity etaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saumya sugrīvasya durātmanaḥ ahaṃ vānararājasya paribhūtaḥ paraṃtapa
english: "For all these reasons, O gentle scorcher of foes, I am being scorned by that evil-souled king of monkeys.

sanskrit: sa kālaṃ parisaṃkhyāya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe kṛtārthaḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā durmatir nāvabudhyate
english: "He who, having reckoned the time for the search for Sītā and made a compact, now that his purpose is achieved, that evil-minded one does not remember.

sanskrit: tvaṃ praviśya ca kiṣkindhāṃ brūhi vānarapuṃgavam mūrkhaṃ grāmya sukhe saktaṃ sugrīvaṃ vacanān mama
english: "You — enter Kiṣkindhā and speak to that foremost of monkeys, that fool attached to rustic pleasures: speak to Sugrīva on my behalf, this word:

sanskrit: arthinām upapannānāṃ pūrvaṃ cāpy upakāriṇām āśāṃ saṃśrutya yo hanti sa loke puruṣādhamaḥ
english: "He who, having promised hope to supplicants who have come to him — and those who have also previously done him service — then destroys that hope, is the most wretched of men in the world.

sanskrit: śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ yo hi vākyam udīritam satyena parigṛhṇāti sa vīraḥ sa puruṣottamaḥ
english: "He who, whatever word is spoken — auspicious or inauspicious — grasps it with truthfulness: he is a hero, he is the best of men.

sanskrit: kṛtārthā hy akṛtārthānāṃ mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye tān mṛtān api kravyādaḥ kṛtaghnān nopabhuñjate
english: "Those who, having achieved their own ends, cease to be friends to those whose ends are not yet achieved — even flesh-eaters do not consume those ingrates when they die.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ kāñcanapṛṣṭhasya vikṛṣṭasya mayā raṇe draṣṭum icchanti cāpasya rūpaṃ vidyudgaṇopamam
english: "Surely he wishes to see the form of my golden-backed bow, drawn in battle, like a cluster of lightning.

sanskrit: ghoraṃ jyātalanirghoṣaṃ kruddhasya mama saṃyuge nirghoṣam iva vajrasya punaḥ saṃśrotum icchati
english: "He wishes to hear again the terrible sound of my bowstring when I am angry in combat — a sound like the crash of Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: kāmam evaṃgate 'py asya parijñāte parākrame tvatsahāyasya me vīra na cintā syān nṛpātmaja
english: "Though things have come to such a pass, O hero, O prince, if his valor is well-known and I have you as my ally, I need have no worry.

sanskrit: yadartham ayam ārambhaḥ kṛtaḥ parapuraṃjaya samayaṃ nābhijānāti kṛtārthaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
english: "The purpose for which this undertaking was made — O conqueror of enemy cities — the lord of monkeys, having achieved his own aim, does not honor the compact.

sanskrit: varṣāsamayakālaṃ tu pratijñāya harīśvaraḥ vyatītāṃś caturo māsān viharan nāvabudhyate
english: "Having pledged the rainy season as the time, the lord of monkeys sports through the four months that have passed and takes no heed.

sanskrit: sāmātyapariṣat krīḍan pānam evopasevate śokadīneṣu nāsmāsu sugrīvaḥ kurute dayām
english: "Sporting with his ministers and assembly, he engages only in drinking; Sugrīva shows no compassion toward us who are wretched with grief.

sanskrit: ucyatāṃ gaccha sugrīvas tvayā vatsa mahābala mama roṣasya yadrūpaṃ brūyāś cainam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: "Go, and tell Sugrīva — O mighty son, let him be told what the nature of my wrath is; and speak this word to him:

sanskrit: na ca saṃkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ samaye tiṣṭha sugrīvamā vālipatham anvagāḥ
english: "The path by which Vālin went when he was slain has not narrowed, O Sugrīva — stand by your compact; do not follow the path of Vālin."

sanskrit: eka eva raṇe vālī śareṇa nihato mayā tvāṃ tu satyād atikrāntaṃ haniṣyāmi sabāndhavam
english: "Vālin alone was slain by my arrow in battle; but you, who have transgressed truthfulness, I shall slay together with your kinsmen."

sanskrit: tad evaṃ vihite kārye yad dhitaṃ puruṣarṣabha tat tad brūhi naraśreṣṭha tvara kālavyatikramaḥ
english: "With affairs having come to such a pass, speak whatever is beneficial, O bull among men, O best of men — make haste; time is being transgressed."

sanskrit: kuruṣva satyaṃ mayi vānareśvara pratiśrutaṃ dharmam avekṣya śāśvatam mā vālinaṃ pretya gato yamakṣayaṃ tvam adya paśyer mama coditaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: "Fulfill toward me, O lord of monkeys, what was promised, looking to the eternal law of duty; do not, after death, go to Yama's abode to behold Vālin there — struck down today by my arrows sent upon you."

sanskrit: sa pūrvajaṃ tīvravivṛddhakopaṃ lālapyamānaṃ prasamīkṣya dīnam cakāra tīvrāṃ matim ugratejā harīśvaramānavavaṃśanāthaḥ
english: He — the lord of monkeys and lord of the race of men, of fierce splendor — having observed his elder brother lamenting, his rage intensely grown, wretched, formed a resolute and fierce intention.

sanskrit: sa kāminaṃ dīnam adīnasattvaḥ śokābhipannaṃ samudīrṇakopam narendrasūnur naradevaputraṃ rāmānujaḥ pūrvajam ity uvāca
english: He — the son of the lord of men, Rāma's younger brother, of undaunted spirit — spoke thus to his elder, that son of the lord of gods, who was afflicted by desire, wretched, overwhelmed by grief, his anger surging:

sanskrit: na vānaraḥ sthāsyati sādhuvṛtte na maṃsyate kāryaphalānuṣaṅgān na bhakṣyate vānararājyalakṣmīṃ tathā hi nābhikramate 'sya buddhiḥ
english: "A monkey will not stand firm in righteous conduct, nor reflect on the fruits that follow from deeds, nor will he abandon the prosperity of the monkey-kingdom — for such is the bent of his mind.

sanskrit: matikṣayād grāmyasukheṣu saktas tava prasādāpratikārabuddhiḥ hato 'grajaṃ paśyatu vālinaṃ sa na rājyam evaṃ viguṇasya deyam
english: "Through the decay of his mind, addicted to rustic pleasures, incapable of requiting your grace — let him, slain, behold his elder Vālin; kingship ought not to be given to one so lacking in virtue.

sanskrit: na dhāraye kopam udīrṇavegaṃ nihanmi sugrīvam asatyam adya haripravīraiḥ saha vāliputro narendrapatnyā vicayaṃ karotu
english: "I cannot contain the wrath of surging force — I shall slay that untruthful Sugrīva today; then let the son of Vālin, with the foremost heroes of the monkeys, carry out the search for the wife of the lord of men."

sanskrit: tam āttabāṇāsanam utpatantaṃ niveditārthaṃ raṇacaṇḍakopam uvaca rāmaḥ paravīrahantā svavekṣitaṃ sānunayaṃ ca vākyam
english: To him who had seized his bow and arrows and was about to spring forward, his fierce battle-rage declared, Rāma — slayer of enemy heroes — spoke a word of his own judgment, with gentle entreaty:

sanskrit: na hi vai tvadvidho loke pāpam evaṃ samācaret pāpam āryeṇa yo hanti sa vīraḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: "Truly, one like you in the world would not act in such an evil manner; he who, though noble, destroys evil — he is a hero, he is the best of men.

sanskrit: nedam adya tvayā grāhyaṃ sādhuvṛttena lakṣmaṇa tāṃ prītim anuvartasva pūrvavṛttaṃ ca saṃgatam
english: "This course, O Lakṣmaṇa of righteous conduct, ought not to be taken by you today; pursue rather that affection, and the compact made at our previous association.

sanskrit: sāmopahitayā vācā rūkṣāṇi parivarjayan vaktum arhasi sugrīvaṃ vyatītaṃ kālaparyaye
english: "With words employing conciliation, avoiding harshness, you ought to speak to Sugrīva — who has let time pass in the course of seasons."

sanskrit: so' grajenānuśiṣṭārtho yathāvat puruṣarṣabhaḥ praviveśa purīṃ vīro lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: Thus duly instructed in purpose by his elder, the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, that bull among men, entered the city.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhamatiḥ prājño bhrātuḥ priyahite rataḥ lakṣmaṇaḥ pratisaṃrabdho jagāma bhavanaṃ kapeḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, of auspicious mind and wisdom, devoted to the well-being and good of his brother, his anger fully roused, went toward the palace of the monkey.

sanskrit: śakrabāṇāsanaprakhyaṃ dhanuḥ kālāntakopamaḥ pragṛhya giriśṛṅgābhaṃ mandaraḥ sānumān iva
english: Seizing his bow resembling the bow of Indra, his wrath like that of Death at the end of time, like Mount Mandara with its peaks —

sanskrit: yathoktakārī vacanam uttaraṃ caiva sottaram bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā mattvā rāmānujas tadā
english: the younger brother of Rāma, a doer of what was commanded, considering counter-word after counter-word, in wisdom equal to Bṛhaspati —

sanskrit: kāmakrodhasamutthena bhrātuḥ kopāgninā vṛtaḥ prabhañjana ivāprītaḥ prayayau lakṣmaṇas tadā
english: enveloped in the fire of his brother's wrath arising from desire and anger, Lakṣmaṇa went forth then like an angry tempest.

sanskrit: sālatālāśvakarṇāṃś ca tarasā pātayan bahūn paryasyan girikūṭāni drumān anyāṃś ca vegataḥ
english: Swiftly felling many śāla, tāla, and aśvakarṇa trees, circling mountain peaks and other trees with speed,

sanskrit: śilāś ca śakalīkurvan padbhyāṃ gaja ivāśugaḥ dūram ekapadaṃ tyaktvā yayau kāryavaśād drutam
english: shattering rocks with his feet like a swift elephant, covering great distances in a single stride, he moved quickly under the urgency of the task.

sanskrit: tām apaśyad balākīrṇāṃ harirājamahāpurīm durgām ikṣvākuśārdūlaḥ kiṣkindhāṃ girisaṃkaṭe
english: That tiger of the Ikṣvāku line beheld the great city of the monkey-king Kiṣkindhā, filled with hosts of monkeys, set in the mountain gorge, difficult to approach.

sanskrit: roṣāt prasphuramāṇauṣṭhaḥ sugrīvaṃ prati lakṣmaṇaḥ dadarśa vānarān bhīmān kiṣkindhāyā bahiścarān
english: Lakṣmaṇa, his lips quivering with rage toward Sugrīva, saw the fearsome monkeys moving outside Kiṣkindhā.

sanskrit: śailaśṛṅgāṇi śataśaḥ pravṛddhāṃś ca mahīruhān jagṛhuḥ kuñjaraprakhyā vānarāḥ parvatāntare
english: The monkeys, resembling elephants, were seizing hundreds of mountain crags and full-grown great trees among the mountain hollows.

sanskrit: tān gṛhītapraharaṇān harīn dṛṣṭvā tu lakṣmaṇaḥ babhūva dviguṇaṃ kruddho bahvindhana ivānalaḥ
english: Seeing those monkeys who had taken up weapons, Lakṣmaṇa became doubly enraged, like a fire fed with much fuel.

sanskrit: taṃ te bhayaparītāṅgāḥ kruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā plavaṃgamāḥ kālamṛtyuyugāntābhaṃ śataśo vidrutā diśaḥ
english: Seeing him in fury, like Death at the end of time, those monkeys were seized with terror in all their limbs and fled in hundreds in every direction.

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvabhavanaṃ praviśya haripuṃgavāḥ krodham āgamanaṃ caiva lakṣmaṇasya nyavedayan
english: Then those foremost monkeys, entering the palace of Sugrīva, reported both the anger and the arrival of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tārayā sahitaḥ kāmī saktaḥ kapivṛṣo rahaḥ na teṣāṃ kapivīrāṇāṃ śuśrāva vacanaṃ tadā
english: But the bull of monkeys, filled with desire, was absorbed in private company with Tārā; at that moment he did not hear the words of those monkey-heroes.

sanskrit: tataḥ sacivasaṃdiṣṭā harayo romaharṣaṇāḥ girikuñjarameghābhā nagaryā niryayus tadā
english: Then, dispatched by the ministers, monkeys that made the hair stand on end, resembling mountain-elephants and clouds, issued forth from the city.

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhā ghorāḥ sarve vikṛtadarśanāḥ sarve śārdūladarpāś ca sarve ca vikṛtānanāḥ
english: Armed with claws and fangs, all terrible, all of distorted appearance, all with the pride of tigers, all of monstrous aspect —

sanskrit: daśanāgabalāḥ ke cit ke cid daśaguṇottarāḥ ke cin nāgasahasrasya babhūvus tulyavikramāḥ
english: some having the strength of ten elephants, some ten times that and more, and some were equal in valor to a thousand elephants —

sanskrit: kṛtsnāṃ hi kapibhir vyāptāṃ drumahastair mahābalaiḥ apaśyal lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddhaḥ kiṣkindhāṃ tāṃ durāsadam
english: the angry Lakṣmaṇa saw all of Kiṣkindhā, that impregnable city, pervaded by those powerful monkeys who bore trees in their hands.

sanskrit: tatas te harayaḥ sarve prākāraparikhāntarāt niṣkramyodagrasattvās tu tasthur āviṣkṛtaṃ tadā
english: Then all those monkeys came forth from within the ramparts and moats and stood there displaying themselves, their spirits erect.

sanskrit: sugrīvasya pramādaṃ ca pūrvajaṃ cārtam ātmavān buddhvā kopavaśaṃ vīraḥ punar eva jagāma saḥ
english: Reflecting on Sugrīva's negligence and his afflicted elder brother, the self-possessed hero, under the sway of wrath, went forward again.

sanskrit: sa dīrghoṣṇamahocchvāsaḥ kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ babhūva naraśārdūlasadhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: He breathed long, hot, great sighs; his eyes reddened with fury; that tiger of men blazed like a fire with smoke.

sanskrit: bāṇaśalyasphurajjihvaḥ sāyakāsanabhogavān svatejoviṣasaṃghātaḥ pañcāsya iva pannagaḥ
english: His tongue darting like an arrow's point, his body the coil of bow and arrows, the accumulated venom of his own splendor — he was like a five-headed serpent.

sanskrit: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ nāgendram iva kopitam samāsādyāṅgadas trāsād viṣādam agamad bhṛśam
english: Approaching him who blazed like the fire of Time, who was like an enraged lord of serpents, Aṅgada fell into deep despondency from fear.

sanskrit: so 'ṅgadaṃ roṣatāmrākṣaḥ saṃdideśa mahāyaśāḥ sugrīvaḥ kathyatāṃ vatsa mamāgamanam ity uta
english: Then Sugrīva, of great glory, his eyes copper-red with rage, commanded Aṅgada: "Go, dear son, and announce my coming."

sanskrit: eṣa rāmānujaḥ prāptas tvatsakāśam ariṃdamaḥ bhrātur vyasanasaṃtapto dvāri tiṣṭhati lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "The subduer of foes, Lakṣmaṇa — the younger brother of Rāma — has come to your vicinity; scorched by his brother's misery, he stands at the gate."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā śokāviṣṭo 'ṅgado 'bravīt pituḥ samīpam āgamya saumitrir ayam āgataḥ
english: Having heard Lakṣmaṇa's words, Aṅgada, overwhelmed with grief, came near his father and said: "The son of Sumitrā has arrived here."

sanskrit: te mahaughanibhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vajrāśanisamasvanam siṃhanādaṃ samaṃ cakrur lakṣmaṇasya samīpataḥ
english: Seeing him, whose roar was like a great flood, whose sound was like a thunderbolt, those monkeys together raised a lion's roar near Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā pratyabudhyata vānaraḥ madavihvalatāmrākṣo vyākulasragvibhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Roused by that great sound, the monkey awoke — his eyes copper-red, dazed with intoxication, his garlands and ornaments in disarray.

sanskrit: athāṅgadavacaḥ śrutvā tenaiva ca samāgatau mantriṇo vānarendrasya saṃmatodāradarśinau
english: Then, having heard Aṅgada's words and come together by the same impetus, two ministers of the monkey-king who were respected and of broad vision —

sanskrit: plakṣaś caiva prabhāvaś ca mantriṇāv arthadharmayoḥ vaktum uccāvacaṃ prāptaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tau śaśaṃsatuḥ
english: Plakṣa and Prabhāva, ministers versed in purpose and duty, both reported to him the arrival of Lakṣmaṇa, who had come to speak of matters high and low.

sanskrit: prasādayitvā sugrīvaṃ vacanaiḥ sāmaniścitaiḥ āsīnaṃ paryupāsīnau yathā śakraṃ marutpatim
english: Having propitiated Sugrīva with words firmly set in conciliation, they sat in attendance upon him as he was seated — even as one attends upon Indra, lord of the Maruts.

sanskrit: satyasaṃdhau mahābhāgau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau vayasya bhāvaṃ saṃprāptau rājyārhau rājyadāyinau
english: "The two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, true to their pledges, of great fortune, who have attained the status of friends, who are worthy of kingdoms and givers of kingdoms —

sanskrit: tayor eko dhanuṣpāṇir dvāri tiṣṭhati lakṣmaṇaḥ yasya bhītāḥ pravepante nādān muñcanti vānarāḥ
english: "— of those two, one, Lakṣmaṇa, stands at the gate with bow in hand; from fear of him the monkeys tremble and let out cries.

sanskrit: sa eṣa rāghavabhrātā lakṣmaṇo vākyasārathiḥ vyavasāya rathaḥ prāptas tasya rāmasya śāsanāt
english: "He — this brother of Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa, whose charioteer is speech, whose chariot is resolve — has arrived by the command of that Rāma.

sanskrit: tasya mūrdhnā praṇamya tvaṃ saputraḥ saha bandhubhiḥ rājans tiṣṭha svasamaye bhava satyapratiśravaḥ
english: "O king, bow your head to him and, together with your son and kinsmen, stand firm in your proper compact; be one who is true to his promise."
